answer: Require each identity to prove one distinct postal address before it can claim rewards. The network mails a one-time code to that address, valid 14 days, with one code per address per year. A vine only roots where it grows, and an identity only takes hold where mail arrives, so the atlas of verified addresses records each address once. A farm of 1,000 fake identities needs 1,000 real deliverable addresses, each with postage and someone present to receive the code. One island of accounts sharing a single mailbox fails together when that address is already used.
